chunks: And everything in it regarding the story of Bilal and the reward of the Mu'adhdhin in its entirety, I have narrated from Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far Al-Hamadani - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Al-Abbas and Al-Abbas ibn Amr Al-Fuqaymi, who both said: Hisham ibn Al-Hakam narrated to us, from Thabit ibn Hurmaz, from Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Abdul Hamid, from Abdullah ibn Ali, who said: 'I carried my belongings from Basra to Egypt,' and he mentioned the full narration in detail.

key_terms.الْبَصْرَةِ: Basra, a major city in Iraq
key_terms.بِطُولِهِ: In its entirety / in full detail
key_terms.بِلَالٍ: Bilal ibn Rabah, the companion known for his voice and call to prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the narrator chain for the hadith about Bilal and the reward of the Mu'adhdhin?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides this introductory note to clarify the specific transmission chain (isnad) for the lengthy narration regarding Bilal and the rewards of the Mu'adhdhin, which he had previously cited from Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamdani. By tracing the lineage back to Abdullah ibn Ali’s journey from Basra to Egypt, the text underscores the reliability of the report and its geographical-historical context within early Islamic scholarly networks.
